samples.summary: 'the caret position always states its reading' asserts two statically-fixed constants, not wrap-boundary behaviour
samples.evidence: Line 116 asserts `lineAffinity === 'backward'` right after `caretAt()`, but `Cursor.moveTo` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:55) hardcodes `affinity ?? pos.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'`, so this holds for any implementation, including one that never computes affinity. Line 121 asserts `'forward'` after ArrowRight, but `text-editor.ts:2770` sets `hAffinity = direction === 'right' ? 'forward' : 'backward'` unconditionally — offset 5→6 in WRAPPED_TEXT is not a wrap boundary, and the comment added by this delta (lines 117-119) now concedes exactly that ("which only matters when that offset is a wrap boundary"), replacing the older comment that claimed the move landed at one. The test does still prove the field rides on the position object, but it no longer exercises the wrap-boundary reading its name and comment describe; a horizontal move at a real boundary would be the meaningful case.

samples.summary: No test covers the vertical-move / shift+Arrow affinity branch that the suite's own comments describe
samples.evidence: `handleArrow` has a distinct branch for vertical moves (`isVertical ? this.cursor.lineAffinity : hAffinity`, text-editor.ts:2775 and 2795) where the affinity comes from `moveVertical`/`paginatedPixelToPosition` rather than a constant — this is the only arrow path whose affinity is layout-derived. In caret-line-affinity.test.ts ArrowDown is only ever used as a setup step (lines 134, 160, 191) and the asserted affinity always comes from the subsequent Home press (text-editor.ts:2818, hardcoded 'forward'). Likewise only shift+Home is asserted (line 164-169); shift+ArrowRight/Down focus affinity (line 2778) is unasserted. So a regression that dropped affinity on vertical or shift+arrow moves would not fail any test here.

mergedFrom.summary: restoreLocalCursor now spreads the resolved position's affinity, but every existing test calls it without one

finding.summary: The undo/redo presence-restore path that now carries lineAffinity has no test
finding.evidence: editor.ts undo (≈2030) and redo (≈2062) were changed from `cursor.moveTo({blockId, offset})` to `cursor.moveTo({...restoredPos, offset})` — a real behavior change (restored caret keeps its wrap-boundary reading). No test enters that branch: it is gated on `'getPresenceCursorPos' in docStore`, and grep shows `getPresenceCursorPos` exists only in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (plus its own test) — MemDocStore, used by every docs view test including the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts, has no such method (grep in packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts: no matches). The frontend store test only covers presence bookkeeping, not the editor's cursor restore. Duplicated code in two places, so both copies are untested.

verdict.reason: The behavior change is real: editor.ts:2035-2038 (undo) and 2067-2070 (redo) now spread the restored presence position ({...restoredPos, offset}) instead of rebuilding {blockId, offset}, so a restored caret keeps its lineAffinity. No test asserts that. The reviewer's sub-claim "no test enters that branch" is inaccurate — editor-undo-selection.test.ts:114 and editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:118,143 drive the real editor over YorkieDocStore (which defines getPresenceCursorPos at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2917), so those lines do execute. But their assertions are insensitive to the change: the first checks getActiveSelection() (restored by the separate restoreSelectionFromPresence path, asserting a range that carries no lineAffinity), the second checks fontSize values only; both pass whether or not the affinity is carried. The only affinity-aware undo test is store-level (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:425-433), which pins getPresenceCursorPos's return value, not the editor's consumption of it. caret-line-affinity.test.ts uses MemDocStore (line 78) and never calls undo/redo. I searched globally for getPresenceCursorPos and lineAffinity, and read every undo/redo test in packages/docs/test and packages/frontend/tests; none would fail if the spread were reverted in either copy. A shipped behavior change with no meaningful test is major under the test-adequacy rubric.
